acceptance: resolve_* is the only lookup API; no float-returning variant remains
Quantity lookups (Fabric SKU, Firebolt node, Databricks warehouse size) return the same resolution type as price lookups
Every lookup strips whitespace before matching; a probe shows 'F2048 ' resolves to 2048 CU, not 2
A designed bucket (sa-east-1 -> other) does NOT set fallback_used; a catch-all guess (BigQuery africa-south1 -> other) DOES
No code path returns 0.0 cost as a consequence of a failed lookup
Tests cover both over-trigger (a valid non-US region stays available) and under-trigger (an unknown key is flagged)
context: Plan: /Users/joe/.claude/plans/stateful-purring-axolotl.md (PR B, Step 1) - see "Revised fail-closed specification" for the per-function table. Raised as top risk by agy; quantity-lookup gap found independently by muse and agy.
description:
Today a missing lookup key silently resolves to a plausible default and the resulting cost is published with cost_status "normalized" - the status that asserts the number is trustworthy.

Introduce a single PriceResolution result type in pricing.py (value, table, resolved_key, fallback_used, unit, reason) and make it the only lookup API - no float-returning twin, so no caller can silently opt out. Convert the get_* functions to resolve_*.

Critically, this must cover NON-PRICE quantity lookups too, which both external reviewers flagged as missing from the original design: pricing.py:302 unknown Fabric SKU -> F2 (2 CU), pricing.py:319 unknown Firebolt node -> M (16 FBU/hr), integration.py:476 unknown Databricks warehouse size -> 2.0 DBU/hr. These multiply into compute_cost exactly like a price; a mistyped f1024 prices as F2, a 512x underbill.

A blanket "KeyError means fallback" rule does not work, because the functions use three different lookup mechanisms. Use the per-function disposition table in the plan. The load-bearing distinction: resolving into a designed, deliberately priced bucket is NOT a fallback (_map_region_to_tier -> "other"; Redshift known-node/unknown-region -> "other"), but a catch-all guess IS (BigQuery unmatched location -> "other" at 5.50 is a guess, not a priced region). Getting this wrong in either direction is the main risk - too strict makes every non-US run unavailable, too loose leaves the defect in place.

Add .strip() before every match. The previous session fixed padded values at the single extraction choke point, but callers that bypass extraction still hit unstripped lookups: 'F2048 ' currently resolves to F2.

On fallback the calculator must still return a QueryCost - returning None would make calculate_phase_cost sum to 0.0, which reads as free and is worse than wrong - but stamp pricing_details["price_unavailable"].
